assumptions: Onset was placed at 15:09 UTC from the metrics and logs; the alert did not fire until 15:13:58 UTC, so customer impact started earlier than the alert window suggests and the stated alert duration understates the impact period.

The causal link between the flag and the failures is inferred from timing plus the error signature: ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:32 appears in the logs only from the minute the flag began evaluating on, and disappears once the flag is reverted. No code-level reproduction or test was run to confirm the defect.

The absence of a recent deploy is taken from the change-event query for this service only; a change elsewhere (e.g. upstream data shape making the divisor zero) was not ruled out, though it was not needed to explain the failures.

A low, steady background rate of `UpstreamTimeout: payment authorization timed out` errors on the account page was present before, during and presumably after the incident. It was treated as pre-existing noise unrelated to this incident and was not investigated.

Exactly how the flag was rolled out (who enabled it, whether it was a percentage ramp or targeting change, and whether it was intentional) was not established — only that the flag provider recorded one recent change to it.

Recovery is based on the service returning to its prior baseline after the revert; no independent check was made that in-flight or queued customer requests during the window were not left in a bad state.
The proposed fix is an unreviewed draft pull request and has not been shown to resolve the defect.
input.executive_summary: On 16 September 2026, customers trying to view their account page on the online shop started getting errors instead of the page. The failures began when a new spending-summary feature was switched on for traffic — partially just after 15:08 UTC and for all traffic from 15:09 UTC — and stopped after the feature was switched back off at 15:14 UTC, with the service confirmed healthy again at 15:15 UTC. Customers who did not open their account page during that window were unaffected, and nothing else about the shop (browsing, checkout) was touched by this. Automated monitoring raised the alert at 15:13 UTC; the response was handled end to end by the automated on-call system, which identified the newly enabled feature as the trigger, reverted it, and verified recovery. The underlying code defect that the feature exposed remains in the codebase; a draft pull request proposing a fix has been opened, and the feature should stay off until that fix is reviewed, merged and verified.
input.root_cause: A feature flag (`monthly-spend-feature`) was switched on for io-shop, which began exercising a code path containing a latent divide-by-zero bug at `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32`; account-page requests that hit that path failed with `ZeroDivisionError`. The flag change was the trigger — no deploy or release was recorded for the service in the 24 hours before onset, so the defective code was already in production but unreachable while the flag was off.
